title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The Authority of Scripture means the Bible is God’s Word and therefore carries God’s own authority over what believers should believe, teach, and obey.
summary: The Authority of Scripture means the Bible is God’s Word and therefore carries God’s own authority over what believers should believe, teach, and obey.
christFocus: Jesus honored Scripture as the Word of God, fulfilled Scripture through His life, death, and resurrection, and taught His followers to live by every word that comes from God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture has authority because it comes from God. The Bible is not merely a collection of religious thoughts, human opinions, or spiritual advice. It is God-breathed truth, given by the Holy Spirit through chosen servants so God’s people could know Him, trust Him, and walk in His ways.

When Scripture speaks clearly, believers are called to receive it with humility. God’s Word corrects false thinking, exposes sin, teaches truth, comforts the weak, warns the careless, and equips the faithful. The authority of Scripture does not crush believers; it anchors them.

Jesus lived under the authority of Scripture. When tempted, He answered with God’s Word. When teaching, He explained God’s Word. After His resurrection, He showed that the Scriptures pointed to Him. The authority of Scripture leads us to Christ because the Bible reveals who He is, what He has done, and how His people are called to follow Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers are pressured to decide truth by feelings, wounds, culture, spiritual experiences, or personal desires. The authority of Scripture gives them a voice higher than fear, shame, addiction, disappointment, human approval, or church manipulation.

God has not left His people guessing. He has spoken. His Word is trustworthy when life feels uncertain, when obedience is difficult, and when the world calls evil good and good evil.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive Scripture as God’s Word, not merely helpful advice. Bring your beliefs, habits, fears, decisions, and desires under what God has spoken, and when Scripture corrects you, let the Lord lead you toward repentance, faith, healing, obedience, and deeper trust in Christ.
